title: How many values can two, three and five make?
description: The numbers two, three and five are used once each, with plus, minus and brackets, to make as many different values as possible. The video finds all six values and shows why there are no others.
teaching_notes: Let the child try first, then compare. One idea: flipping the sign of a number lowers the total by twice that number. Ask the child to list their own expressions before comparing.

video_script.why: The child makes expressions from three numbers with plus, minus and brackets, and sees that the sign of each number decides the value.
video_script.substitution: The same method works with other three numbers: start from the total and flip signs.
video_script.anchor: the numbers two, three and five on cards, with plus, minus and bracket cards
video_script.payoff_line: The possible values are ten, six, four, zero, minus four and minus six.

final_answer.value: Many answers; the possible values are 10, 6, 4, 0, −4 and −6
final_answer.spoken: many answers are possible, and the possible values are ten, six, four, zero, minus four and minus six

maths_rules: starting from 10, flipping the sign of a number lowers the value by twice that number: flip 2 gives 6, flip 3 gives 4, flip 5 gives 0, flip 2 and 3 gives 0, flip 2 and 5 gives -4, flip 3 and 5 gives -6
flipping all three would give -10, which cannot be made because the first number cannot be negative
the possible values are 10, 6, 4, 0, -4 and -6; 10 is the largest, using all plus signs

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to make as many different values as possible.

marks.m1: the order 2, 3, 5 is written with no brackets

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, start with no brackets, in the order two, three, five.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Two plus three plus five is ten.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Two plus three minus five is zero.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Two minus three plus five is four, and two minus three minus five is minus six.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, try other orders, and brackets.
Three plus five minus two is six.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Three minus five minus two is minus four.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Three minus the bracket five minus two is zero.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Five minus the bracket three minus two is four.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: start from 10; flipping a sign lowers the value by twice the number: flip 2 → 6; flip 3 → 4; flip 5 → 0; flip 2 and 3 → 0; flip 2 and 5 → −4; flip 3 and 5 → −6; flip all three → −10, not possible

marks.m1: 10 is written as the starting total
marks.m2: flip 2, flip 3 and flip 5 are written with 6, 4 and 0
marks.m3: flip 2 and 3, 2 and 5, and 3 and 5 are written with 0, −4 and −6
marks.m4: flip all three → −10 is written and crossed out

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, see why only these values come out.
Start from ten, where every number is added.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Flipping the sign of a number lowers the value by twice that number.
Flipping two gives six, flipping three gives four, and flipping five gives zero.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Flipping two numbers together gives zero, minus four or minus six.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Flipping all three would give minus ten, but the first number cannot be made negative.

marks.m1: 5 − (3 − 2) = 5 − 1 = 4 is written and matched with the flip rule
marks.m2: 2 − (3 + 5) = 2 − 8 = −6 is written and matched with the flip rule

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, check two of them.
Five minus the bracket three minus two is five minus one, which is four.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Two minus the bracket three plus five is two minus eight, which is minus six.
